standard_prerequisites.name: The extended Cech complex of an open covering of a topological space
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the definition of the Cech complex with its term in degree -1 given by F(U); the statement refers to the extended complex explicitly
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the complex and its indexing, including the convention U_{i_0 ... i_p} = U_{i_0} cap ... cap U_{i_p}; the homotopy is the counted content.

standard_prerequisites.name: Contracting homotopies of cochain complexes
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard homological algebra: a homotopy h with dh + hd = id exhibits the complex as homotopy equivalent to zero
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the shape of the verification performed in the proof.

core_obligations: Exploit the repeated index: fix i with U_i = U and observe that U_{i_0 ... i_p} = U_{i_0 ... hat i_j ... i_p} whenever i_j = i, so inserting the index i into a tuple does not change the intersection (proof lines 963-964).

Define the homotopy: set h(s)_{i_0 ... i_p} = s_{i i_0 ... i_p} on the products of sections of the Cech terms, i.e. h is the projection onto the factors of tuples starting with i, which in degree -1 is the projection prod_{i_0} F(U_{i_0}) -> F(U) onto the factor F(U_i) = F(U) (proof lines 965-980).

Verify the contraction: compute (dh + hd)(s)_{i_0 ... i_p} by expanding the two sums, and observe that the terms with the inserted index cancel because of the opposite signs (-1)^j and (-1)^{j+1}, leaving exactly s_{i_0 ... i_p}, so the identity map of the complex is homotopic to zero (proof lines 981-1003).
proof_roadmap: Use the hypothesis U_i = U to see that the index i can be inserted or deleted from a tuple without changing the corresponding intersection (proof lines 963-964).
Define the homotopy h by prefixing tuples with the index i and interpret it degree by degree as a projection (proof lines 965-980).
Compute dh + hd and cancel the summed terms to obtain the identity, which gives the homotopy equivalence with zero (proof lines 981-1003).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if an open covering of a topological space contains the whole space as one of its members, then the extended Cech complex with F(U) placed in degree -1 is homotopy equivalent to zero (statement lines 950-959). The proof produces the contracting homotopy explicitly, by prefixing every tuple of indices with the distinguished index i and reading the resulting map as a projection onto the factors F(U_{i i_1 ...}) = F(U_{i_1 ...}); the verification is then a displayed cancellation of two sums of sections with opposite signs (proof lines 963-1003). The step that has to be seen rather than cited is that prefixing with the repeated index changes nothing on the intersections, so that the homotopy is well defined at all. The claim is H2: one explicit homotopy and one computation.
